Python Overview and Installation

The Python version of ATOM SDK is an official client library that interacts with the ATOM background service (atom_vp_interface). It encapsulates the underlying HTTP communication into a clearly typed Python interface. The complete process of graph creation, node configuration, parameter setting, graph running, etc. can be completed with a small amount of code.

Features

  • The parameter object uses dataclass, with field names and default values clearly visible.

  • The Service method returns the normal Python type, allowing for direct processing of JSON, list, byte, and point cloud results.

  • AtomClient shares timestamp among all Service to reduce editing version conflicts.

  • Runtime supports normal EPICRAW, passive binocular EPICRAW3 and single-node direct running.

Installation

First download atom_sdk_<version>.zip from the Download Center and extract it. The Python wheel is in <SDK_DIR>/python/.

# Optional: create and activate a virtual environment
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate          # Windows PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# Install the downloaded wheel
python -m pip install <SDK_DIR>/python/atom_sdk-<version>-*.whl

Choose a wheel that matches your Python version and operating system. To change versions, download the corresponding archive from the Download Center and install it again.

Big Four Service at a glance

Service attributes Class name Responsibilities

client.graph

GraphService

Main picture life cycle management: create, open, run, import and export diagrams

client.node

NodeService

Main graph node operations: create nodes, connect lines, set parameters, activate nodes

client.graph_node

GraphNodeService

subgraph node operation: enter a graph node to internally manage the nodes in its subgraph

client.runtime

RuntimeService

Runtime execution: Load graph in execution engine mode and submit sensor frame data

When to use which service?

  • Build graph structure (new nodes, connections, parameter adjustments) → client.graph + client.node

  • Operation subgraph internal node → client.graph_node

  • Call Atom as an inference engine (only need to feed data and get results) → client.runtime

When doing external business integration, use client.runtime first; only when you need to build a diagram, change nodes, or maintain a template diagram, use client.graph / client.node / client.graph_node.

AtomClient

AtomClient is the unified entrance of SDK. All Service instances are built during initialization and share the same timestamp cache internally.

Import method

from atom_sdk import AtomClient

Construction parameters

AtomClient(base_url, transport=None, options=None)

Name Type Description

base_url

str

atom_vp_interface Service address, for example http://127.0.0.1:10026. There is no need to add a slash at the end, SDK will be removed automatically.

transport

BaseTransport | None

Optional. Custom transport layer. When not passed, RequestsTransport is used by default, implemented based on the requests library. Commonly used to inject mock in unit tests.

options

RequestOptions | None

Optional. Default request configuration, such as timeouts and common request headers. If not passed, the built-in default value of the library will be used.

RequestOptions fields:

Field Type Default value Description

timeout

float

30.0

Timeout seconds for each request

headers

dict[str, str]

{}

Public request headers that will be included in every request

Instance properties

Access individual services through the following properties:

Attribute Type Description

client.graph

GraphService

Main image management service (create, open, run, import and export images)

client.node

NodeService

Main graph node service (create node, connect, set parameters, activate)

client.graph_node

GraphNodeService

Subgraph Node Service (operates subgraph nodes inside graph node)

client.runtime

RuntimeService

Runtime execution service (execute graph in inference engine mode)

client.base_url

str

The service address currently used by the client (the trailing slash has been removed)

client.timestamps

TimestampStore

internal timestamp cache (usually not needed directly)

Advanced usage

Custom timeout

from atom_sdk import AtomClient
from atom_sdk.core.models import RequestOptions

options = RequestOptions(timeout=60.0)  # The timeout is set to 60 seconds
client = AtomClient(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:10026", options=options)

Inject mock transport layer in test

from atom_sdk import AtomClient
from atom_sdk.core.transport import BaseTransport

class MockTransport(BaseTransport):
    def request(self, method, path, **kwargs):
        # Return mock response
        ...

client = AtomClient(base_url="http://localhost", transport=MockTransport())

Connect to remote service

# Connected to the LAN Atom service
client = AtomClient(base_url="http://192.168.1.100:10026")

# Verify the connection is normal
graphs = client.graph.list_graphs()
print(f"Currently there are {len(graphs)} Picture")

  • AtomClient is not thread-safe. If used in a multi-threaded environment, it is recommended to create a separate instance for each thread.

  • TimestampStore is shared among all services, and operations of the graph_node service update the timestamp cache shared with the node service.

  • The slash at the end of base_url will be automatically removed, and http://127.0.0.1:10026/ and http://127.0.0.1:10026 have the same effect.

Things to note

  • AtomClient is not thread-safe, and multi-threaded environments recommend creating a separate instance for each thread.

  • TimestampStore is shared among all Service; operations on graph_node update timestamp shared with node.

  • The slash at the end of base_url will be automatically removed, and the effect is the same with or without a slash.

Common entrances

Attribute Type Use

client.graph

GraphService

Create, open, import, export and run master images

client.node

NodeService

Edit main graph node

client.graph_node

GraphNodeService

Edit graph node Internal submap

client.runtime

RuntimeService

Load graph, feed data and read inference results

If you are unsure which entry should be used, see Service 选择.

Return value convention

SDK will first check the business status returned by the server: if it is not 0, it will throw AtomApiError; if it is successful and the business result is an ordinary dictionary, status will be retained in the returned dictionary, which is convenient for you to record logs or determine whether this request is successful. Lists, Boolean values, strings, primitive bytes, and point cloud analysis results will maintain their original types, and the structure will not be changed to add state.

Quick example

from atom_sdk import AtomClient, CreateGraphParams, CreateNodeParams

client = AtomClient(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:10026")

# Create diagram
graph = client.graph.create_graph(CreateGraphParams("my_graph"))
print("Create graph request status:", graph["status"])

# open diagram(SDK Automatic caching timestamp)
client.graph.open_graph("my_graph")

# Create nodes in the graph
result = client.node.create_node(CreateNodeParams("my_graph", "DetectAndSegment"))
print("Request status:", result["status"])
node_id = result["nodeId"]

# Run chart
run_result = client.graph.run_graph("my_graph")
print("Run request status:", run_result["status"])
